questions.text:
Which of the following statements about parser is/are CORRECT?
I. Canonical LR is more powerful than SLR.
II. SLR is more powerful than LALR
III. SLR is more powerful than Canonical LR.
questions.solution:
Power of LR parsers: LR(0) [latex]\lt[/latex] SLR [latex]\lt[/latex] LALR [latex]\lt[/latex] Canonical LR. So only "Canonical LR is more powerful than SLR" is correct.

Answer: I only

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are shared by all the threads in a process ?
I. Program counter
II. Stack
III. Address space
IV. Registers
questions.solution:
Each thread has its own program counter, stack and registers. All threads of a process share the address space (code, data, heap, open files).

Answer: III only

questions.text:
In a file allocation system, which of the following allocation schemes(s) can be used if no external fragmentation is allowed?
I. Contiguous
II. Linked
III. Indexed
questions.solution:
Contiguous allocation needs one big continuous hole, which causes external fragmentation. Linked and indexed allocation can use any free block anywhere, so they have no external fragmentation.

Answer: II and III only

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the routing protocols, Routing Information Protocol (RIP) and Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) in an IPv4 network.

I. RIP uses distance vector routing
II. RIP packets are sent using UDP
III. OSPF packets are sent using TCP
IV. OSPF operation is based on link-state routing

Which of the statements above are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- RIP is distance-vector True and runs over UDP (port 520) True
- OSPF is link-state True, but runs directly over IP (protocol 89), not TCP False

Answer: I, II and IV only

questions.text: If [latex]f(x)=R sin(\frac{\pi x}{2})+S,f'(\frac{1}{2})=\sqrt{2}[/latex] and [latex] \int_{0}^{1}f(x)dx=\frac{2R}{\pi }[/latex], then the constants R and S are, respectively
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]f'(x)=\frac{R\pi}{2}\cos\frac{\pi x}{2}[/latex], so [latex]f'(\tfrac12)=\frac{R\pi}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{\sqrt2}=\sqrt2\Rightarrow R=\frac4\pi[/latex]
- [latex]\int_0^1f\,dx=R\cdot\frac2\pi+S[/latex]. This equals [latex]\frac{2R}{\pi}[/latex], so S = 0.

Answer: [latex]\frac4\pi[/latex] and 0
